issuer.summary: PRIME's own issuer is Hastra (Signum Ltd.), which is unregulated — the SEC registration a reader is likely to notice belongs to Figure Certificate Company, the entity underneath the wrapper. FCC is a genuine full reporting registrant, KPMG-audited with a clean annual opinion and 100.3% ICA §28 coverage, its parent listed on Nasdaq as FIGR. Two limits hold this below the top of the range: the interim going-concern conclusion depends on parent support rather than standing alone, and the issuer can freeze holder balances. See the full report for the audit scope, reserve proofs and freeze authorities.

facts: ⚠️ THE REGISTRATION IS ONE LAYER DOWN. This axis scores Figure Certificate Company; PRIME's own issuer is Hastra (Signum Ltd.), UNREGULATED. A reader seeing 'SEC registrant, KPMG-audited' is reading about the asset underneath the wrapper, not the wrapper they hold.
✅ Figure Certificate Company is a full SEC reporting registrant: 10-K/10-Q with officer certifications, KPMG-audited since 2024, clean opinion, no going-concern qualification, no material weakness.
✅ Investment Company Act §28 requires qualified assets above the certificate reserve plus minimum capital. FCC disclosed 100.3% coverage at 2026-03-31.
✅ Parent Figure Technology Solutions trades on Nasdaq as FIGR.

⚠️ The clean audit opinion covers only the ANNUAL statements. The interim filing's going-concern conclusion is CONDITIONAL ON PARENT SUPPORT — a commitment letter to pay invoices and periodically forgive intercompany balances — not an independent conclusion.
⚠️ The issuer can FREEZE holder balances: mint and freeze authorities are program PDAs post-init, with freeze administrable by up to five admins. Program upgrade sits behind a Squads v4 multisig.
✅ Live proof-of-reserves at hastra.io/proof-of-reserves shows wYLDS 100.31% backed, with Provenance-chain reserve wallets independently verifiable.

✅ Two audit firms have covered the stack: Informal Systems (Solana vault-mint/stake, Nov 2025 — 1 Critical plus a vault-inflation follow-up) and Sherlock (Solana + Ethereum full stack and the cross-chain price path, Apr 2026 — 0 Critical / 0 High, 2 Medium resolved, 2 Medium accepted).

⚠️ NOT priced on this axis: PRIME is predominantly a collateral asset and the systemic-leverage question is recorded on Structural, per this desk's rule that the Liquidity axis scores observed depth only.

⚠️ PROCESS NOTE, kept because it explains a past divergence: this score was published for months with no internal source — the published report's 6.5 had no upstream and the producer feed independently hardcoded 5.5, a value matching no published figure. the published report remains the authoring surface; the two must move together.

⚠️⚠️ FCC'S MAJORITY REPO COUNTERPARTY CHANGED, AND IT IS A CHANGE IN KIND. At 2026-06-30 Schedule I lists TWO repo counterparties: Hidden Road Partners CIV US LLC $200,000K (70.8%) and UMB Bank N.A. $82,361K (29.2%). At 2026-03-31 UMB was the SOLE repo counterparty at $389,556K and the Hidden Road facility was documented but UNUSED — 'no investment transactions had been executed under the arrangement'. So a DORMANT FACILITY WAS DRAWN TO $200M IN ONE QUARTER while UMB fell 79%. ✅ Hidden Road is identifiable and the answer runs OPPOSITE to what an unnamed counterparty implies: SEC broker-dealer #8-71259, CRD #331954, FINRA/SIPC member, CFTC-registered FCM, audited by RSM US LLP, ultimate parent RIPPLE LABS INC. since 2025-10-21 per its own X-17A-5 (CIK 0002029588). $39.02B assets against $520.4M member's equity — 75:1, but reverse repo $38.183B against repo $37.770B is a MATCHED BOOK, not a directional position, and FCC's $200M is 0.51% of it. Repo is Treasury-collateralised. ⚠️ THE FINDING IS CORRELATION, NOT CREDIT: a bank with discount-window access and FDIC insurance was replaced as majority repo counterparty by a CRYPTO-OWNED NON-BANK, for an issuer whose product is a blockchain-native security. A broker-dealer has neither backstop and SIPC does not cover repo exposure. ⚠️ Do NOT write this as a quality concern about the counterparty — that would overstate risk. [riskAnalyst, FCC Q2 10-Q + HRP X-17A-5, 2026-09-13]

⚠️⚠️ FCC'S OUTSIDE DEMAND IS SHRINKING AND THE CONCENTRATION HEADLINE HIDES IT. Certificates by holder, three dates: 2025-12-31 related $252,282K / third-party $75,911K / total $328,193K (76.9% related); 2026-03-31 $472,990K / $125,057K / $598,047K (79.1%); 2026-06-30 $477,536K / $78,497K / $556,033K (85.9%). ⚠️ Q1→Q2 THE THIRD-PARTY LEG FELL 37.2% AND THE TOTAL BOOK SHRANK 7.0%, while related-party grew just +1.0%. THE RISE FROM 79.1% TO 85.9% IS ALMOST ENTIRELY THIRD-PARTY REDEMPTION, NOT AFFILIATE GROWTH. ⚠️ MEASURED AGAINST THE Q2 FILING'S OWN COMPARATIVE COLUMN (2025-12-31) THE THIRD-PARTY LEG READS FLAT AT +3.4% — that window spans two quarters and hides a quarter in which the retail book redeemed more than a third of itself. riskAnalyst published the +3.4% version first and corrected it the same day. ALWAYS QUOTE THE THREE-DATE SERIES. [riskAnalyst, FCC Q1 + Q2 10-Qs, 2026-09-13]

⚠️ CUSTODY IS NOT SINGLE-NAME AND ONE LEG IS AFFILIATE-HELD. Schedule V at 2026-06-30: UMB Bank N.A. $555,722K (securities), Lead Bank $5,488K (cash), Flagstar Bank N.A. $700K (cash), total $561,910K. UMB is sole custodian of the SECURITIES but NOT the sole depositary. ⚠️ Footnote (2): 'The Lead Bank account is held by Figure Pay and includes amounts related to affiliated entities. The amount disclosed represents only the portion attributable to FCC.' So 1.0% of qualified assets sits in a COMMINGLED AFFILIATE ACCOUNT with FCC's share set by ALLOCATION rather than segregation — a custody fact, and the §28 deposit requirement is an asset test. ⚠️ Schedule V total $561,910K and the balance-sheet 'qualified assets' $561,627K differ by exactly the $283K separately-stated interest receivable; they are different measures, not a discrepancy. [riskAnalyst, FCC Q2 10-Q, 2026-09-13]
